record.original_question: Given real vector spaces V1,...,Vd with dim(Vi)=ni+1, does there exist a tensor T ∈ V1⊗···⊗Vd such that all c(n) critical points (equivalently singular tuples in the cited setup) are real?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Given real vector spaces V1 , . . . , Vd with dim Vi = ni + 1, does there exist a tensor T ∈ V1 ⊗ · · · ⊗ Vd such that T has c(n) critical points defined over the real numbers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V_1,\dots,V_d$ be real vector spaces with $\dim V_i = n_i+1$, and write $\mathbf{n}=(n_1,\dots,n_d)$. Equip each $V_i$ with the standard inner product, and equip $V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ with the induced inner product. A singular vector tuple (equivalently, a critical rank-one tuple) of a tensor $T\in V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ is a tuple of nonzero vectors $(v_1,\dots,v_d)\in V_1\times\cdots\times V_d$, considered up to simultaneous rescaling, that is a critical point of the function $(v_1,\dots,v_d)\mapsto \langle T,\,v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d\rangle$ restricted to the product of unit spheres $S(V_1)\times\cdots\times S(V_d)$. For a generic tensor $T$ over the complex numbers, the number of complex singular vector tuples is a finite constant $c(\mathbf{n})$ depending only on $\mathbf{n}$, given by an explicit formula of Friedland–Ottaviani.

Question: Does there exist a real tensor $T\in V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ all of whose $c(\mathbf{n})$ singular vector tuples are real (i.e., such that every complex critical point is in fact defined over $\mathbb{R}$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of total reality of singular vector tuples of tensors (analogous to real eigenvalue problems / real enumerative geometry) appears to be an active open question in tensor decomposition / applied algebraic geometry. Recent works (e.g., on decomposing tensors via rank-one approximations and on the span of singular tuples) treat related aspects but do not report a resolution of whether a real tensor with all $c(\mathbf{n})$ singular tuples real exists in general formats.

status_evidence.title: Decomposing tensors via rank-one approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses singular vector tuples and rank-one approximations of tensors with no claim of resolution of the total-reality problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate singular tuples without settling the existence of totally real tensors.

status_evidence.title: The number of singular vector tuples and uniqueness of best rank one approximation of tensors
status_evidence.snippet: Gives the formula c(n) for the number of complex singular vector tuples of a generic tensor.
status_evidence.claim: The count c(n) of complex singular tuples is established, but reality of all c(n) tuples is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The span of singular tuples of a tensor beyond the boundary format
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometric properties of singular tuples beyond boundary format.
status_evidence.claim: Related work that does not resolve the reality problem.
